title: How Telarus Expands Veea’s Multi-Channel Sales Engine
summary: Veea is building a multi-channel, partner-led sales engine around one common edge platform. Our Technology Services Distribution Agreement with Telarus adds an established technology-advisor channel to that strategy.
body_markdown:
# **Building partner-led distribution for the intelligent business location**


Technology reaches scale through distribution.


Veea is building a multi-channel, partner-led sales engine around one common edge platform. Our Technology Services Distribution Agreement with Telarus adds an established technology-advisor channel to that strategy.


Through the agreement, Telarus’ extensive network of technology advisors and channel partners gains access to Veea’s secure connectivity, cybersecurity, intelligent networking, edge computing and AI-enabled solutions.


Telarus brings established customer relationships, channel expertise and experience across communications, cloud, cybersecurity and networking. Veea brings an integrated platform designed to support a growing portfolio of services at the business edge.


Together, that creates an established route for bringing Veea technology into customer conversations already taking place across small and medium-sized businesses and distributed enterprises.


### **Distribution is a strategic capability**


Enterprise technology is rarely purchased as an isolated product.


A customer considering a networking upgrade may also be evaluating cybersecurity, cloud services, communications, video, IoT or a broader infrastructure-modernization program.


Technology advisors help customers navigate those decisions. They understand the operating environment, the business requirements and the broader technology portfolio that must work together.


Telarus has spent more than two decades building an ecosystem around those customer needs. Its advisors help businesses source, purchase and implement technologies across communications, cloud, cybersecurity, networking and other critical categories.


Veea fits naturally within that model.


The VeeaONE platform brings connectivity, computing, cybersecurity and intelligent applications together in one edge architecture. It can support secure connectivity, SD-WAN, Zero Trust security, IoT, video intelligence, edge computing and AI-enabled services.


For an advisor already helping a customer address networking, security or infrastructure challenges, Veea creates an opportunity to address more of that customer’s technology needs through the same underlying platform.


### **Begin with customer outcomes**


Businesses do not need to begin by adopting an abstract technology category. They can begin with an immediate operational need.


A distributed enterprise may need to secure multiple locations.


A retailer may need to separate payment, employee, guest and operational traffic.


A business may want to add cameras, sensors or intelligent applications without introducing another disconnected system.


An organization exploring AI may need a secure environment for processing real-world data locally.


These are practical entry points for the Veea platform.


A customer can begin with secure connectivity, cybersecurity or networking. The same managed environment can then support IoT monitoring, video intelligence, operational automation and local AI as requirements evolve.


This is especially relevant for small and medium-sized businesses and distributed enterprises. These organizations need capable, secure infrastructure, but they may not have large IT teams available at every location.


Veea gives technology advisors a platform for bringing those capabilities together and managing them consistently across sites.


### **One platform with complementary channels**


Veea’s route-to-market strategy is designed around multiple complementary channels.


Telecommunications operators can combine Veea capabilities with connectivity and managed services.


Systems integrators can bring the platform into specialized industries and operating environments.


Technology advisors can introduce Veea as part of broader customer strategies spanning networking, cloud, cybersecurity, communications and AI.


Each route reaches the market differently while building on a common platform.


In Mexico, the Telcel relationship has advanced an operator model over 5G into commercial service and customer billing. The Totalplay relationship is advancing another operator path over fiber, with technical qualification complete and commercial planning continuing.


Telarus adds an established technology-advisor and distribution channel. It brings Veea into business conversations led by partners that already understand their customers’ infrastructure, service and operational priorities.


The access point may differ, but the commercial model is consistent: package the capabilities of one platform into relevant services and bring those services to market through partners with established customer relationships, sales expertise and support infrastructure.


### **What Telarus adds**


The Technology Services Distribution Agreement establishes a commercial framework through which Telarus advisors can bring Veea solutions to their customers.


That framework supports the work of enabling advisors, developing customer opportunities, placing orders, deploying solutions and building recurring services.


For Veea, this expands commercial reach through a channel designed to serve customers across a wide range of technology requirements.


For Telarus advisors, Veea adds an integrated platform that can address multiple infrastructure priorities through a common operating environment.


For customers, the result is a practical path to secure and modernize business locations without assembling and managing a separate infrastructure stack for every new capability.


This alignment is central to the model.


Veea expands its access to the market. Advisors gain more ways to create value for their customers. Businesses gain technology that is easier to deploy, secure and manage.


### **More value from every business location**


The opportunity extends beyond a single transaction.


A customer may begin with managed connectivity, cybersecurity or networking across multiple locations. Over time, that same customer may add cameras, sensors, IoT monitoring, operational intelligence, edge computing or AI-enabled applications.


Because those capabilities can operate through the same edge environment, partners can expand the services delivered to a location without replacing the underlying platform.


This creates opportunities for advisors to build recurring revenue around managed connectivity, cybersecurity, edge computing and intelligent applications.


It also gives Veea a distribution model through which one deployed platform can support a broader portfolio of services as customer requirements develop.


### **From connectivity to intelligence**


Business locations are becoming increasingly intelligent.


Cameras are becoming operational sensors. Connected devices are producing larger volumes of real-world data. Cybersecurity is moving closer to where that data is created. AI applications increasingly need to analyze information and respond locally.


These applications require more than an AI model. They require secure connectivity, computing, deployment, management and support.


Veea is designed to provide the edge infrastructure that brings those capabilities together.


Customers can begin with the priorities they have today and add more intelligent services over time. Partners can meet those evolving requirements through a common platform rather than a growing collection of disconnected systems.


### **Building commercial reach**


The Telarus agreement adds another important component to Veea’s partner-led sales engine.


Veea brings a common edge platform designed to support secure connectivity and increasingly intelligent services.


Telarus brings channel expertise, distribution capabilities and an established ecosystem of technology advisors.


Together, the companies can make Veea technology available where customers are already evaluating and purchasing connectivity, cybersecurity, networking, cloud and edge solutions.


That is the commercial objective: meet customers through trusted channels, solve immediate business problems and create a foundation for expanding services across more locations and applications.


**One platform. More services. More routes to market. Commercial progress that builds.**
